The preparation of ALD 60 SnO and IZO thin-films was detailed in another previous study by NREL.160 2 Following the as-synthesized characterizations at NREL, PSC samples were packaged in a vacuum bag in an inert environment (i.e., glove box) and shipped to Hawaii Natural Energy Institute (HNEI) via FedEx 2-day shipping. Upon delivery at HNEI, the samples were placed in a nitrogen glove box (box pressure approx. 1.2 mbar, ultra-high purity N : 2 99.999%, Oxygen Level < 0.1 ppm, Moisture Level < 0.5 ppm) and liberated from the vacuum seal. To form the semi-bonded TCC on PSCs, the freshly prepared composite mixture was drop-cast directly onto the PSC in the glove box, and placed under a vacuum in the glove box’s load lock for de-gassing for 10 minutes. The samples were transferred back into the glove box and compressed under a compliant substrate for overnight curing. The compliant substrate comprised a rubber gasket between a polypropylene release film and a glass substrate, effectively reducing the lamination pressure (approx. 0.4 bar). The encapsulated PSCs were packaged in a vacuum bag inside the glove box and shipped back to NREL (FedEx 2-day shipping) typically within three weeks of being received. Finally at NREL, a secondary IZO layer (thickness: 230 nm) was deposited directly on the TCC layer by reactive sputtering in an argon and oxygen atmosphere, leading to the final encapsulated structure (IZO/TCC/IZO/SnO /C /Cs FA MA Pb(I Br ) /MeO- 2 60 0.05 0.85 0.10 0.97 0.03 3 2PACZ/ITO/Glass). The control samples, synthesized from the same batch as the encapsulated PSCs and remained at NREL in a nitrogen-filled glovebox until the 35/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard encapsulated PSCs returned, at which point their electrical characterization and durability testing were conducted concurrently. The current density-voltage (J-V) characterizations of PSCs were measured in an N 2 glovebox using an AM 1.5G solar simulator (Oriel Sol3A Class AAA) using the terminating IZO layer and the ITO back contact as electrical contacts. The intensity of the solar simulator was calibrated to 100 mW/cm2 using a reference silicon solar cell (Oriel, VLSI standards, certified by NREL PV Performance Calibration group). Stabilities of encapsulated PSCs and control samples were tested under 1-sun illumination from a sulfur plasma lamp (sample surface temp. approx. 50˚C) in ambient air (40-60% R.H.) while being held under a resistive load near the maximum power point (560 Ω). Subtask 2.1: Electrical testing of encapsulated PSC devices: Unprotected and encapsulated cells were tested continuously near their maximum power point (“quasi- MPP” technique) in a laboratory at 50 °C, in air (40-60% R.H.), 1-sun intensity.
